hero.title: Web3 with JavaScript and Node.js: from first read to full application
hero.subtitle: Read the chain, send transactions with care, connect wallets, build a signed-message login, index events into a database and test it all. Every task is checked and explained.
hero.outcomeLine: After this course you can build and test the JavaScript side of a Web3 application.

assessment: Finish the required labs in each module: they are checked automatically and explained when something is missing.
Pass each module quiz (70% or more). Short tests inside the lessons give instant feedback.
Complete the application design and the final assessment.

faq.q: Does the platform run my JavaScript?
faq.a: No. The labs check your designs, calculations and plans. You run the code yourself with Node.js on a local or test network.

faq.q: Which library does the course use?
faq.a: ethers version 6, which is widely used and well documented. The ideas apply to other libraries too.
Yes, if you only use local nodes and test networks with throw-away accounts. Never use a key that controls real funds.

activities.title: What does a transaction really cost?
activities.objective: Turn gas used and gas price into ETH and rupees, and judge whether a feature is affordable.
activities.scenario: Your app sends a transaction that uses 52,000 gas when the gas price is 25 gwei and ETH is 250,000 rupees. (Teaching figures.)
steps: In B7 work out the fee in ETH: gas used times gwei divided by 1,000,000,000.
In B8 convert it to rupees.
In B9 work out the monthly cost for the number of transactions in B5.
In B10 work out the fee if the gas price doubles.
In B11 show Too expensive for a free action if B8 is above the limit in B6, otherwise Acceptable.

checks.label: B7 is the fee in ETH
checks.explain: Gas times gwei over a billion.

checks.label: B8 is the fee in rupees
B9 is the monthly cost
B10 is the doubled fee
checks.hint: Try the formula =B8*2 here.
checks.explain: Double the price, double the fee.

checks.label: B11 is the verdict
checks.hint: =IF(B8>B6,"Too expensive for a free action","Acceptable")

spec.equals: Too expensive for a free action

cells.A6: Most you would pay for a free action (rupees)

activities.title: Plan retries with backoff
activities.objective: Calculate how long a retry plan waits and whether it fits what the user will tolerate.
activities.scenario: When an RPC call fails, your app waits 1 second, then 2, then 4 and so on, doubling each time, for up to 6 attempts. (A teaching model.)
steps: In B7 work out the delay before the last wait: the start delay times 2 to the power of attempts minus 2.
In B8 work out the total waiting time between the 6 attempts: start delay times (2 to the power of attempts minus 1, minus 1).
In B9 show Within limit if B8 is not above the limit in B5, otherwise Give up earlier.
In B10 work out the average wait per attempt.
In B11 work out the delay for attempt 7 if the delays double with no cap.

checks.label: B7 is the last wait
checks.hint: =B2*POWER(B4,B3-2)

checks.label: B8 is the total wait
checks.explain: A doubling series adds up to the next power minus one.

checks.label: B9 is the verdict
checks.hint: =IF(B8>B5,"Give up earlier","Within limit")
checks.explain: Compare with what the user tolerates.

checks.label: B10 is the average wait
B11 is the next delay
checks.hint: =B2*POWER(B4,B3)

activities.title: Why polling from every browser breaks
activities.objective: Compare the request load of client polling with one shared backend that reads each block once.
activities.scenario: 2,000 users keep a page open and each browser asks the RPC provider for data 6 times a minute. A backend could read once per block (about 7,200 blocks a day) and share the results. (A teaching model.)
steps: In B7 work out the requests per day from client polling: users times polls per minute times 60 times 24.
In B8 write the requests per day from one backend: the blocks per day.
In B9 work out the requests saved.
In B10 work out the percentage saved.
In B11 show Client polling exceeds the plan if B7 is above the plan limit in B5, otherwise Fits the plan.

checks.label: B7 is the client load
checks.explain: Users times polls times minutes in a day.

checks.label: B8 is the backend load
checks.hint: Try the formula =B4 here.

checks.label: B9 is the saving
B10 is the percentage
B11 is the verdict
checks.hint: =IF(B7>B5,"Client polling exceeds the plan","Fits the plan")
